strategy.angle: The hidden power bottleneck in AI scaling
strategy.audience: Houston business leaders, energy executives, and industrial operators

draft.hook: The biggest threat to your AI strategy isn't software architecture—it's the limitations of the local power grid.
draft.body:
FERC just issued new guidance to accelerate the interconnection process for large-load consumers like AI data centers and advanced manufacturing facilities. For the Houston business community, this is the signal shift you’ve been waiting for. We are moving from a world of 'queue stagnation' to one where industrial-scale AI infrastructure is being prioritized in national grid planning.

Why does this matter for your bottom line? Because compute is no longer the scarce resource. Power capacity is. If your enterprise plans involve large-scale model deployment or high-compute manufacturing, you are currently competing for electrons in a marketplace that hasn't kept pace with demand.

At Amplify Intelligence, we’ve been tracking how this 'grid-first' mentality changes the competitive landscape. If you aren't factoring energy availability into your 24-month technology roadmap, your scaling plans are effectively DOA. 

How does this impact Houston specifically? Being home to the nation’s energy capital gives us an inherent edge, but only if we pivot from being pure consumers of energy to architects of high-load AI infrastructure. I’ve been discussing this with industry leaders: the firms that integrate power logistics into their digital transformation strategy today will be the ones that avoid the connectivity bottlenecks that will stall their competitors tomorrow.
draft.closing: Leon Coe and the team at Amplify Intelligence are currently stress-testing these energy-load scenarios for regional scale. We aren't just looking at algorithms; we're looking at the infrastructure that keeps them running.
draft.cta: If you are planning an AI rollout that requires industrial-grade compute, are you talking to your regional energy stakeholders, or are you just talking to your software vendors?
